title: OR-12 · Decision making, planning, and control
summary: Select feasible actions under declared objectives and constraints, with decision outcomes evaluated separately from model fit.

goals.title: Define the operation contract
goals.description: Define state, action set, objective, constraints, policy output, environment assumptions and failure or abstention conditions.

milestones.title: Specify inputs, outputs and requirements
milestones.description: Define state, action set, objective, constraints, policy output, environment assumptions and failure or abstention conditions. Create the Operation Contract and linked Requirements-and-Evidence Record before an experiment is admitted. Apply the linked shared admission, compatibility, temporal and evidence rules; the acceptance criteria below define this milestone’s completion boundary.
acceptance: The versioned Operation Contract and linked Requirements-and-Evidence Record specify input/output roles, claim scope, operation parameters, and typed failure or abstention conditions; existing charter links are design references, not evidence that this milestone is complete.

The contract inherits foundations-record-validation, foundations-temporal-integrity, foundations-data-protocol and foundations-lifecycle-admission. Any not-applicable rule is justified; a reusable interface can be drafted before instance selection, but an admitted run binds every required dataset, provider, artifact and protocol dependency.

Declare action authority and whether evaluation is realized, simulated or based on observational policy data. Specify permitted fallbacks, cost/constraint semantics and the identification or simulator scope that supports comparisons; documentation does not authorize live actions.

goals.title: Provide a reference implementation
goals.description: Provide the declared policy or planner with independently testable dynamics dependencies, constraint checks and action provenance.

milestones.title: Implement the agreed operation interface
milestones.description: Provide the declared policy or planner with independently testable dynamics dependencies, constraint checks and action provenance. The method, dataset and implementation slice remain to be selected. Apply the linked shared admission, compatibility, temporal and evidence rules; the acceptance criteria below define this milestone’s completion boundary.
acceptance: Conformance tests exercise the declared role/SpaceRef relationship, applicable temporal checks, malformed or unsupported inputs, stale fitted artifacts and explicit failure propagation; no rejected record becomes an ordinary vector or unreported omission.

Outputs retain parent/source lineage, representation kind, OperationRun identity, code/configuration and fitted-artifact identities. Engineering fixtures are labeled engineering-only and do not establish operation quality.

Keep each action linked to its observation/forecast origin, objective, policy and model versions. A failed upstream result cannot silently become a normal action; a fallback is a separately identified, predeclared path with explicit feasibility checks.

goals.title: Establish operation-specific evidence
goals.description: Compare realized or validly simulated outcomes, costs and violations against appropriate policy baselines; document simulator and identification limits.

milestones.title: Define and execute the admitted evaluation
milestones.description: Compare realized or validly simulated outcomes, costs and violations against appropriate policy baselines; document simulator and identification limits. Freeze the selected protocol, baselines and failure criteria before held-out assessment; retain negative outcomes and limitations. Apply the linked shared admission, compatibility, temporal and evidence rules; the acceptance criteria below define this milestone’s completion boundary.
acceptance: The admitted protocol fixes data partitions, instance and artifact identities, baselines, budgets, selection policy, metrics and failure criteria before held-out assessment. Diagnostic exposure, changes and repeated looks are indexed; a revised protocol does not silently reuse an exposed confirmation set.

Report the declared evaluation unit, uncertainty or its justified limitation, coverage including abstentions and failures, and relevant resource costs. Index every initiated run and its outcome under foundations-evidence-ledger; do not discard unsuccessful or inconclusive evidence.

A valid completed evaluation can be negative or inconclusive. Milestone completion is not a positive claim verdict, and invalid or unexecuted attempts alone cannot satisfy operation-quality evaluation acceptance.

Report decision outcomes, costs, violations, failures and fallback coverage for the entire admitted policy. Do not treat logged outcomes of unchosen actions as observed counterfactuals, or model accuracy as evidence of action value.

goals.title: Expose Hx12 capabilities as a reusable toolset
goals.description: Expose the policy or planner calls, objective and constraint checks, fallback handling, workflow composition and result handling developed within this Hero through common CLI and reusable library interfaces across compatible representation providers. Make functionality discoverable, configurable, checkable, callable and inspectable while preserving operation-owned behavior and explicit composition points. Provider-neutral interfaces do not establish universal compatibility, representation suitability or currently implemented capability.

milestones.title: Define the Hx12 toolset surface
milestones.description: Map the Hero's implemented and selected future building blocks to public tools and reusable APIs. Identify existing interfaces, implementation gaps, ownership, schemas, dependencies and claim limits before agreeing the delivery coverage.
acceptance: A versioned toolset map links each intended public capability to its owning implementation or explicit implementation gap, contract, request/result schemas, prerequisites and supported claim scope.

Document common discover, configure, check, run and inspect workflows through CLI and reusable APIs, including how individual steps compose and how results can be reused. Keep model/provider behavior with its owner and declare the interfaces this Hero consumes.

Declare state and action contracts, objective and cost context, feasibility constraints, policy/model dependencies, fallback semantics and whether use is simulated, observational or live. Interface exposure does not authorize live actions.

evidence.label: Shared CLI and reusable API conventions

milestones.title: Expose and verify the agreed Hx12 building blocks
milestones.description: Deliver the public interfaces and composed workflows agreed in the toolset map, with discoverable commands, documented schemas, reusable results and provider-neutral examples. This planning entry does not admit a new experiment, training run, API call or other external execution.
acceptance: The agreed toolset map has no unreported exposure gaps: selected implemented building blocks and workflows are callable through documented CLI and library interfaces, while unavailable capabilities and compatibility limits remain explicit.

End-to-end engineering examples use the same public calling conventions with distinct compatible provider configurations where applicable, preserve artifact identity and lineage, and retain all failure, abstention and unresolved outcomes. Scientific utility and transfer claims require separate bound evaluation evidence.

Examples retain decision context, policy/model identities, constraints, feasibility outcomes and explicit fallbacks; upstream failure cannot silently become an ordinary action. Policy outcome claims remain separate from model accuracy and preserve simulator or identification limits.

evidence.label: Shared CLI and reusable API conventions
